entries.reason: the header says the QNG and QAG integrators are C ports of the QUADPACK corresponding routines and that QAGS provides the functionality of QAGS and QAGI, so the algorithms, the node tables and the error bookkeeping are QUADPACK's: netlib's dqng.f, dqags.f, dqagse.f, dqagie.f, dqk15.f, dqk15i.f, dqk21.f, dqk31.f, dqk41.f, dqk51.f, dqk61.f, dqelg.f and dqpsrt.f, public domain, transcribed statement for statement, with the six abscissa and weight tables and the four of dqng generated from the Fortran DATA statements rather than typed
entries.effect: the integral of the caller's array callback over the bounds, with the status the header's enumeration names and an estimate of the absolute error in the caller's abs_error; measured against the host on 86 cases - five integrands over three integrators and three intervals, the six point counts the header lists, max_intervals 1 to 3, a workspace of exactly one interval's bytes and one byte less, a bound at infinity, and every refusal - with the answer, the status, the point count, the batch sizes and the batch sizes' order all compared, and the estimate checked against the exact integral of the case rather than against the host's own estimate, which is a cancellation-amplified quantity the host does not reproduce against itself
entries.source: the host's own Accelerate, held against the port case by case by tests/backports/host/quadrature, whose run.sh checks the 29 tables against the DATA statements before it builds anything; netlib's QUADPACK for the algorithms and the tables; the held releases' own exports, whose first rung carrying _quadrature_integrate is 10.0.1 (tools/cache-index/first-rung.lua), so every band below 10.0 carries the object; the object imports only libSystem's fmax, fmin, pow, malloc and free (nm -u at armv7-apple-ios4.3), so its floor is 4.3
